title: Delivery Semantics & Exactly-Once
summary: Networks retry. Exactly-once end-to-end is usually an illusion built from at-least-once delivery plus idempotent processing and transactional boundaries. Design for duplicates explicitly.

sections.title: At-most-once, at-least-once, effectively once
paragraphs: At-most-once drops messages on failure. At-least-once retries until ack — duplicates happen. Exactly-once claims require a precise scope: once within a pipeline stage, once into a sink with idempotent keys, etc.
Kafka transactions, Flink checkpoints, and inbox/outbox patterns create effective once processing relative to a defined side-effect boundary — not magic across the whole enterprise.

sections.title: Idempotency as the real tool
paragraphs: Give producers idempotency keys. Make consumers store processed keys or use natural unique constraints. Upserts beat blind inserts.
Side effects (email, charges) need dedup stores with TTLs aligned to retry windows. Document the window.

sections.title: Transactional messaging patterns
paragraphs: Transactional outbox: write business row + outbox row atomically; publisher drains outbox. Inbox: consumer records message id before side effects.
Dual writes to DB and queue without a transaction are a classic source of lost or double events.

sections.title: What to tell product stakeholders
paragraphs: Say 'at-least-once with idempotent handlers' instead of 'exactly once' unless you can name the boundary and the failure proof.

deepDive.title: Delivery Semantics & Exactly-Once — Operations
paragraphs: Operating Delivery Semantics & Exactly-Once in production means defining SLIs before tuning knobs, knowing amplification costs, and rehearsing failure modes.
Prefer reversible changes, feature flags, and canaries. Measure p50/p99 and error rate under load that matches production skew.
bullets: Define capacity from the scarcest resource
Keep rollback cheaper than forward repair when possible

deepDive.title: Delivery Semantics & Exactly-Once — Failure modes
paragraphs: Common failures around Delivery Semantics & Exactly-Once include overload, partial dependency outages, and silent correctness bugs that pass happy-path tests.
Inject faults in staging: latency, loss, clock skew, and disk full. Verify alerts fire and degradation is intentional.

expert.title: Delivery Semantics & Exactly-Once — Expert notes
paragraphs: At the expert level, Delivery Semantics & Exactly-Once intersects multi-region consistency, cost envelopes, and organizational constraints (team ownership, on-call load).
Write down the non-goals. Many outages come from optimizing a metric that was never the product requirement.

practices: Design consumers to be idempotent first
pitfalls: Believing the broker alone provides exactly-once side effects
Dedup TTLs shorter than max retry duration

keyTakeaways: Idempotency + transactional boundaries create effective once
whyItMatters: Most 'random' production bugs in event-driven systems are duplicate or lost side effects from unclear delivery semantics.
reflectionQuestions: What side effects in your system are not idempotent?
Where do you dual-write today without an outbox?
numbersToKnow: Know your p99 latency budget before adding hops
Peak load ≠ average load — plan headroom (often 2–3×)
Cross-region RTT is often ~50–150ms one way
